topic: Why a block header is 80 bytes
title: Why Every Bitcoin Block Header Is 80 Bytes
hook: Every Bitcoin block header adds up to exactly eighty bytes.

scenes.narration: Version, timestamp, difficulty bits and nonce are four bytes each.
The previous block hash and merkle root are thirty-two bytes each.
That's sixteen plus sixty-four, or eighty, and only the header is hashed.

cta: Did you add it up? Tell me in the comments, and the link is on my channel page.
description_body: 4+4+4+4 plus 32+32 makes the 80-byte header that miners hash.
